title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement: Andy and Bethany have a rectangular array of numbers with \(40\) rows and \(75\) columns. Andy adds the numbers in each row. The average of his \(40\) sums is \(A.\) Bethany adds the numbers in each column. The average of her \(75\) sums is \(B.\) What is the value of \(\dfrac{A}{B}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(S\) be the sum of all numbers in the array.

Andy’s \(40\) row sums also add to \(S,\) so their average is \(A=\dfrac{S}{40}.\) Bethany’s \(75\) column sums also add to \(S,\) so their average is \(B=\dfrac{S}{75}.\)

Therefore \(\dfrac{A}{B}=\dfrac{\frac{S}{40}}{\frac{S}{75}}=\dfrac{75}{40}=\dfrac{15}{8}.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let \(S\) be the sum of all entries in the array.
Andy has average row sum \(\frac{S}{40},\) while Bethany has average column sum \(\frac{S}{75}.\)
